[52](https://docs.rs#52)/// Derive [`Display`].
[53](https://docs.rs#53)///
[54](https://docs.rs#54)/// ## Helper attributes
[55](https://docs.rs#55)///
[56](https://docs.rs#56)/// `#[derive(Display)]` and `#[derive(FromStr)]` use common helper attributes.
[57](https://docs.rs#57)///
[58](https://docs.rs#58)/// - `#[derive(Display)]` use `#[display]`.
[59](https://docs.rs#59)/// - `#[derive(FromStr)]` use both `#[display]` and `#[from_str]`, with `#[from_str]` having priority.
[60](https://docs.rs#60)///
[61](https://docs.rs#61)/// Helper attributes can be written in the following positions.
[62](https://docs.rs#62)///
[63](https://docs.rs#63)/// | attribute                                                     | `#[display]` | `#[from_str]` | struct | enum | variant | field |
[64](https://docs.rs#64)/// | ------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------ | ------------- | ------ | ---- | ------- | ----- |
[65](https://docs.rs#65)/// | [`#[display("...")]`](#display)                               | ✔            |               | ✔      | ✔    | ✔       | ✔     |
[66](https://docs.rs#66)/// | [`#[display(style = "...")]`](#displaystyle--)                | ✔            |               |        | ✔    | ✔       |       |
[67](https://docs.rs#67)/// | [`#[display(with = ...)]`](#displaywith---from_strwith--)     | ✔            | ✔             |        |      |         | ✔     |
[68](https://docs.rs#68)/// | [`#[display(opt)]`](#displayopt)                              |              |               |        |      |         | ✔     |
[69](https://docs.rs#69)/// | [`#[display(bound(...))]`](#displaybound-from_strbound)       | ✔            | ✔             | ✔      | ✔    | ✔       | ✔     |
[70](https://docs.rs#70)/// | [`#[display(crate = ...)]`](#displaycrate--)                  | ✔            |               | ✔      | ✔    |         |       |
[71](https://docs.rs#71)/// | [`#[display(dump)]`](#displaydump-from_strdump)               | ✔            | ✔             | ✔      | ✔    |         |       |
[72](https://docs.rs#72)/// | [`#[from_str(regex = "...")]`](#from_strregex--)              |              | ✔             | ✔      | ✔    | ✔       | ✔     |
[73](https://docs.rs#73)/// | [`#[from_str(regex_infer)]`](#from_strregex_infer)            |              | ✔             | ✔      | ✔    | ✔       | ✔     |
[74](https://docs.rs#74)/// | [`#[from_str(new = ...)]`](#from_strnew--)                    |              | ✔             | ✔      |      | ✔       |       |
[75](https://docs.rs#75)/// | [`#[from_str(ignore)]`](#from_strignore)                      |              | ✔             |        |      | ✔       |       |
[76](https://docs.rs#76)/// | [`#[from_str(default)]`](#from_strdefault)                    |              | ✔             | ✔      |      |         | ✔     |
[77](https://docs.rs#77)///
[78](https://docs.rs#78)/// ## `#[display("...")]`
[79](https://docs.rs#79)///
[80](https://docs.rs#80)/// Specifies the format using a syntax similar to [`std::format!()`].
[81](https://docs.rs#81)///
[82](https://docs.rs#82)/// However, unlike `std::format!()`, `{}` has the following meaning.
[83](https://docs.rs#83)///
[84](https://docs.rs#84)/// | format                | struct | enum | variant | field | description                                                                         |
[85](https://docs.rs#85)/// | --------------------- | ------ | ---- | ------- | ----- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
[86](https://docs.rs#86)/// | [`{a}`, `{b}`, `{1}`] | ✔      | ✔    | ✔       | ✔     | Use a field with the specified name.                                                |
[87](https://docs.rs#87)/// | [`{}`]                |        | ✔    | ✔       |       | Use a variant name of enum.                                                         |
[88](https://docs.rs#88)/// | [`{}`,`{:x}`, `{:?}`] |        |      |         | ✔     | Use the field itself.                                                               |
[89](https://docs.rs#89)/// | [`{:x}`, `{:?}`]      | ✔      | ✔    |         |       | Use format traits other than [`Display`] for `self`. (e.g. [`LowerHex`], [`Debug`]) |
[90](https://docs.rs#90)/// | [`{a.b.c}`]           | ✔      | ✔    | ✔       | ✔     | Use a nested field.                                                                 |
[91](https://docs.rs#91)///
[92](https://docs.rs#92)/// [`LowerHex`]: std::fmt::LowerHex
[93](https://docs.rs#93)/// [`{a}`, `{b}`, `{1}`]: #struct-format
[94](https://docs.rs#94)/// [`{}`]: #variant-name
[95](https://docs.rs#95)/// [`{}`,`{:x}`, `{:?}`]: #field-format
[96](https://docs.rs#96)/// [`{:x}`, `{:?}`]: #format-parameter
[97](https://docs.rs#97)/// [`{a.b.c}`]: #nested-field
[98](https://docs.rs#98)///
[99](https://docs.rs#99)/// ### Struct format
[100](https://docs.rs#100)///
[101](https://docs.rs#101)/// By writing `#[display("..")]`, you can specify the format used by `Display` and `FromStr`.
[102](https://docs.rs#102)///
[103](https://docs.rs#103)/// ```rust
[104](https://docs.rs#104)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[105](https://docs.rs#105)///
[106](https://docs.rs#106)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[107](https://docs.rs#107)/// #[display("{a}-{b}")]
[108](https://docs.rs#108)/// struct MyStruct {
[109](https://docs.rs#109)///   a: u32,
[110](https://docs.rs#110)///   b: u32,
[111](https://docs.rs#111)/// }
[112](https://docs.rs#112)/// assert_eq!(MyStruct { a:10, b:20 }.to_string(), "10-20");
[113](https://docs.rs#113)/// assert_eq!("10-20".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a:10, b:20 }));
[114](https://docs.rs#114)///
[115](https://docs.rs#115)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[116](https://docs.rs#116)/// #[display("{0}+{1}")]
[117](https://docs.rs#117)/// struct MyTuple(u32, u32);
[118](https://docs.rs#118)/// assert_eq!(MyTuple(10, 20).to_string(), "10+20");
[119](https://docs.rs#119)/// assert_eq!("10+20".parse(), Ok(MyTuple(10, 20)));
[120](https://docs.rs#120)/// ```
[121](https://docs.rs#121)///
[122](https://docs.rs#122)/// ### Newtype pattern
[123](https://docs.rs#123)///
[124](https://docs.rs#124)/// If the struct has only one field, the format can be omitted.
[125](https://docs.rs#125)/// In this case, the only field is used.
[126](https://docs.rs#126)///
[127](https://docs.rs#127)/// ```rust
[128](https://docs.rs#128)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[129](https://docs.rs#129)///
[130](https://docs.rs#130)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[131](https://docs.rs#131)/// struct NewType(u32);
[132](https://docs.rs#132)/// assert_eq!(NewType(10).to_string(), "10");
[133](https://docs.rs#133)/// assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(NewType(10)));
[134](https://docs.rs#134)/// ```
[135](https://docs.rs#135)///
[136](https://docs.rs#136)/// ### Enum format
[137](https://docs.rs#137)///
[138](https://docs.rs#138)/// In enum, you can specify the format for each variant.
[139](https://docs.rs#139)///
[140](https://docs.rs#140)/// ```rust
[141](https://docs.rs#141)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[142](https://docs.rs#142)///
[143](https://docs.rs#143)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[144](https://docs.rs#144)/// enum MyEnum {
[145](https://docs.rs#145)///   #[display("aaa")]
[146](https://docs.rs#146)///   VarA,
[147](https://docs.rs#147)///   #[display("bbb")]
[148](https://docs.rs#148)///   VarB,
[149](https://docs.rs#149)/// }
[150](https://docs.rs#150)/// assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA.to_string(), "aaa");
[151](https://docs.rs#151)/// assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarB.to_string(), "bbb");
[152](https://docs.rs#152)/// assert_eq!("aaa".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
[153](https://docs.rs#153)/// assert_eq!("bbb".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarB));
[154](https://docs.rs#154)/// ```
[155](https://docs.rs#155)///
[156](https://docs.rs#156)/// In enum format, `{}` means variant name.
[157](https://docs.rs#157)/// Variant name style (e.g. `snake_case`, `camelCase`, ...) can be specified by [`#[from_str(style = "...")]`](#displaystyle--).
[158](https://docs.rs#158)///
[159](https://docs.rs#159)/// ```rust
[160](https://docs.rs#160)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[161](https://docs.rs#161)///
[162](https://docs.rs#162)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[163](https://docs.rs#163)/// enum MyEnum {
[164](https://docs.rs#164)///   #[display("aaa-{}")]
[165](https://docs.rs#165)///   VarA,
[166](https://docs.rs#166)///   #[display("bbb-{}")]
[167](https://docs.rs#167)///   VarB,
[168](https://docs.rs#168)/// }
[169](https://docs.rs#169)/// assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA.to_string(), "aaa-VarA");
[170](https://docs.rs#170)/// assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarB.to_string(), "bbb-VarB");
[171](https://docs.rs#171)/// assert_eq!("aaa-VarA".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
[172](https://docs.rs#172)/// assert_eq!("bbb-VarB".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarB));
[173](https://docs.rs#173)///
[174](https://docs.rs#174)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[175](https://docs.rs#175)/// #[display(style = "snake_case")]
[176](https://docs.rs#176)/// enum MyEnumSnake {
[177](https://docs.rs#177)///   #[display("{}")]
[178](https://docs.rs#178)///   VarA,
[179](https://docs.rs#179)/// }
[180](https://docs.rs#180)/// assert_eq!(MyEnumSnake::VarA.to_string(), "var_a");
[181](https://docs.rs#181)/// assert_eq!("var_a".parse(), Ok(MyEnumSnake::VarA));
[182](https://docs.rs#182)/// ```
[183](https://docs.rs#183)///
[184](https://docs.rs#184)/// By writing a format on enum instead of variant, you can specify the format common to multiple variants.
[185](https://docs.rs#185)///
[186](https://docs.rs#186)/// ```rust
[187](https://docs.rs#187)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[188](https://docs.rs#188)///
[189](https://docs.rs#189)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[190](https://docs.rs#190)/// #[display("xxx-{}")]
[191](https://docs.rs#191)/// enum MyEnum {
[192](https://docs.rs#192)///   VarA,
[193](https://docs.rs#193)///   VarB,
[194](https://docs.rs#194)/// }
[195](https://docs.rs#195)/// assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA.to_string(), "xxx-VarA");
[196](https://docs.rs#196)/// assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarB.to_string(), "xxx-VarB");
[197](https://docs.rs#197)/// assert_eq!("xxx-VarA".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
[198](https://docs.rs#198)/// assert_eq!("xxx-VarB".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarB));
[199](https://docs.rs#199)/// ```
[200](https://docs.rs#200)///
[201](https://docs.rs#201)/// ### Unit variants
[202](https://docs.rs#202)///
[203](https://docs.rs#203)/// If all variants has no field, format can be omitted.
[204](https://docs.rs#204)/// In this case, variant name is used.
[205](https://docs.rs#205)///
[206](https://docs.rs#206)/// ```rust
[207](https://docs.rs#207)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[208](https://docs.rs#208)///
[209](https://docs.rs#209)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[210](https://docs.rs#210)/// enum MyEnum {
[211](https://docs.rs#211)///   VarA,
[212](https://docs.rs#212)///   VarB,
[213](https://docs.rs#213)/// }
[214](https://docs.rs#214)/// assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA.to_string(), "VarA");
[215](https://docs.rs#215)/// assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarB.to_string(), "VarB");
[216](https://docs.rs#216)/// assert_eq!("VarA".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
[217](https://docs.rs#217)/// assert_eq!("VarB".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarB));
[218](https://docs.rs#218)/// ```
[219](https://docs.rs#219)///
[220](https://docs.rs#220)/// ### Field format
[221](https://docs.rs#221)///
[222](https://docs.rs#222)/// You can specify the format of the field.
[223](https://docs.rs#223)/// In field format, `{}` means the field itself.
[224](https://docs.rs#224)///
[225](https://docs.rs#225)/// ```rust
[226](https://docs.rs#226)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[227](https://docs.rs#227)///
[228](https://docs.rs#228)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[229](https://docs.rs#229)/// #[display("{a}, {b}")]
[230](https://docs.rs#230)/// struct MyStruct {
[231](https://docs.rs#231)///   #[display("a is {}")]
[232](https://docs.rs#232)///   a: u32,
[233](https://docs.rs#233)///   #[display("b is {}")]
[234](https://docs.rs#234)///   b: u32,
[235](https://docs.rs#235)/// }
[236](https://docs.rs#236)/// assert_eq!(MyStruct { a:10, b:20 }.to_string(), "a is 10, b is 20");
[237](https://docs.rs#237)/// assert_eq!("a is 10, b is 20".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a:10, b:20 }));
[238](https://docs.rs#238)///
[239](https://docs.rs#239)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[240](https://docs.rs#240)/// #[display("{0}, {1}")]
[241](https://docs.rs#241)/// struct MyTuple(#[display("first is {}")] u32, #[display("next is {}")] u32);
[242](https://docs.rs#242)/// assert_eq!(MyTuple(10, 20).to_string(), "first is 10, next is 20");
[243](https://docs.rs#243)/// assert_eq!("first is 10, next is 20".parse(), Ok(MyTuple(10, 20)));
[244](https://docs.rs#244)///
[245](https://docs.rs#245)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[246](https://docs.rs#246)/// enum MyEnum {
[247](https://docs.rs#247)///   #[display("this is A {0}")]
[248](https://docs.rs#248)///   VarA(#[display("___{}___")] u32),
[249](https://docs.rs#249)/// }
[250](https://docs.rs#250)/// assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA(10).to_string(), "this is A ___10___");
[251](https://docs.rs#251)/// assert_eq!("this is A ___10___".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA(10)));
[252](https://docs.rs#252)/// ```
[253](https://docs.rs#253)///
[254](https://docs.rs#254)/// ### Format parameter
[255](https://docs.rs#255)///
[256](https://docs.rs#256)/// Like `std::format!()`, format parameter can be specified.
[257](https://docs.rs#257)///
[258](https://docs.rs#258)/// ```rust
[259](https://docs.rs#259)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[260](https://docs.rs#260)///
[261](https://docs.rs#261)/// #[derive(Display, PartialEq, Debug)]
[262](https://docs.rs#262)/// #[display("{a:>04}")]
[263](https://docs.rs#263)/// struct WithFormatParameter {
[264](https://docs.rs#264)///   a: u32,
[265](https://docs.rs#265)/// }
[266](https://docs.rs#266)/// assert_eq!(WithFormatParameter { a:5 }.to_string(), "0005");
[267](https://docs.rs#267)/// ```
[268](https://docs.rs#268)///
[269](https://docs.rs#269)/// When `{}` is used within `#[display("...")]` set for an enum, and if a format trait is added to `{}` such as `{:?}`, the meaning changes from "variant name" to "a string using a trait other than Display for self."
[270](https://docs.rs#270)///
[271](https://docs.rs#271)/// ```rust
[272](https://docs.rs#272)/// use parse_display::Display;
[273](https://docs.rs#273)///
[274](https://docs.rs#274)/// #[derive(Display, PartialEq, Debug)]
[275](https://docs.rs#275)/// #[display("{}")]
[276](https://docs.rs#276)/// enum X {
[277](https://docs.rs#277)///   A,
[278](https://docs.rs#278)/// }
[279](https://docs.rs#279)/// assert_eq!(X::A.to_string(), "A");
[280](https://docs.rs#280)///
[281](https://docs.rs#281)/// #[derive(Display, PartialEq)]
[282](https://docs.rs#282)/// #[display("{:?}")]
[283](https://docs.rs#283)/// enum Y {
[284](https://docs.rs#284)///   A,
[285](https://docs.rs#285)/// }
[286](https://docs.rs#286)/// impl std::fmt::Debug for Y {
[287](https://docs.rs#287)///   fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter) -> std::fmt::Result {
[288](https://docs.rs#288)///     write!(f, "Debug Y")
[289](https://docs.rs#289)///   }
[290](https://docs.rs#290)/// }
[291](https://docs.rs#291)/// assert_eq!(Y::A.to_string(), "Debug Y");
[292](https://docs.rs#292)/// ```
[293](https://docs.rs#293)///
[294](https://docs.rs#294)/// ### Nested field
[295](https://docs.rs#295)///
[296](https://docs.rs#296)/// You can use nested field, e.g. `{x.a}` .
[297](https://docs.rs#297)///
[298](https://docs.rs#298)/// ```rust
[299](https://docs.rs#299)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[300](https://docs.rs#300)///
[301](https://docs.rs#301)/// #[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Default)]
[302](https://docs.rs#302)/// struct X {
[303](https://docs.rs#303)///     a: u32,
[304](https://docs.rs#304)///     b: u32,
[305](https://docs.rs#305)/// }
[306](https://docs.rs#306)///
[307](https://docs.rs#307)/// #[derive(FromStr, Display, PartialEq, Debug)]
[308](https://docs.rs#308)/// #[display("{x.a}")]
[309](https://docs.rs#309)/// struct Y {
[310](https://docs.rs#310)///     #[from_str(default)]
[311](https://docs.rs#311)///     x: X,
[312](https://docs.rs#312)/// }
[313](https://docs.rs#313)/// assert_eq!(Y { x: X { a: 10, b: 20 } }.to_string(), "10");
[314](https://docs.rs#314)/// assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(Y { x: X { a: 10, b: 0 } }));
[315](https://docs.rs#315)/// ```
[316](https://docs.rs#316)///
[317](https://docs.rs#317)/// When using nested field, you need to use [`#[from_str(default)]`](#from_strdefault) to implement `FromStr`.
[318](https://docs.rs#318)///
[319](https://docs.rs#319)/// ## `#[display(style = "...")]`
[320](https://docs.rs#320)///
[321](https://docs.rs#321)/// By writing `#[display(style = "...")]`, you can specify the variant name style.
[322](https://docs.rs#322)/// The following styles are available.
[323](https://docs.rs#323)///
[324](https://docs.rs#324)/// - `none`
[325](https://docs.rs#325)/// - `lowercase`
[326](https://docs.rs#326)/// - `UPPERCASE`
[327](https://docs.rs#327)/// - `snake_case`
[328](https://docs.rs#328)/// - `SNAKE_CASE`
[329](https://docs.rs#329)/// - `camelCase`
[330](https://docs.rs#330)/// - `CamelCase`
[331](https://docs.rs#331)/// - `kebab-case`
[332](https://docs.rs#332)/// - `KEBAB-CASE`
[333](https://docs.rs#333)/// - `Title Case`
[334](https://docs.rs#334)/// - `Title case`
[335](https://docs.rs#335)/// - `title case`
[336](https://docs.rs#336)/// - `TITLE CASE`
[337](https://docs.rs#337)///
[338](https://docs.rs#338)/// ```rust
[339](https://docs.rs#339)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[340](https://docs.rs#340)///
[341](https://docs.rs#341)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[342](https://docs.rs#342)/// #[display(style = "snake_case")]
[343](https://docs.rs#343)/// enum MyEnum {
[344](https://docs.rs#344)///   VarA,
[345](https://docs.rs#345)///   VarB,
[346](https://docs.rs#346)/// }
[347](https://docs.rs#347)/// assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA.to_string(), "var_a");
[348](https://docs.rs#348)/// assert_eq!("var_a".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
[349](https://docs.rs#349)///
[350](https://docs.rs#350)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[351](https://docs.rs#351)/// enum StyleExample {
[352](https://docs.rs#352)///   #[display(style = "none")]
[353](https://docs.rs#353)///   VarA1,
[354](https://docs.rs#354)///   #[display(style = "none")]
[355](https://docs.rs#355)///   varA2,
[356](https://docs.rs#356)///   #[display(style = "lowercase")]
[357](https://docs.rs#357)///   VarB,
[358](https://docs.rs#358)///   #[display(style = "UPPERCASE")]
[359](https://docs.rs#359)///   VarC,
[360](https://docs.rs#360)///   #[display(style = "snake_case")]
[361](https://docs.rs#361)///   VarD,
[362](https://docs.rs#362)///   #[display(style = "SNAKE_CASE")]
[363](https://docs.rs#363)///   VarE,
[364](https://docs.rs#364)///   #[display(style = "camelCase")]
[365](https://docs.rs#365)///   VarF,
[366](https://docs.rs#366)///   #[display(style = "CamelCase")]
[367](https://docs.rs#367)///   VarG1,
[368](https://docs.rs#368)///   #[display(style = "CamelCase")]
[369](https://docs.rs#369)///   varG2,
[370](https://docs.rs#370)///   #[display(style = "kebab-case")]
[371](https://docs.rs#371)///   VarH,
[372](https://docs.rs#372)///   #[display(style = "KEBAB-CASE")]
[373](https://docs.rs#373)///   VarI,
[374](https://docs.rs#374)///   #[display(style = "Title Case")]
[375](https://docs.rs#375)///   VarJ,
[376](https://docs.rs#376)///   #[display(style = "Title case")]
[377](https://docs.rs#377)///   VarK,
[378](https://docs.rs#378)///   #[display(style = "title case")]
[379](https://docs.rs#379)///   VarL,
[380](https://docs.rs#380)///   #[display(style = "TITLE CASE")]
[381](https://docs.rs#381)///   VarM,
[382](https://docs.rs#382)/// }
[383](https://docs.rs#383)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarA1.to_string(), "VarA1");
[384](https://docs.rs#384)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::varA2.to_string(), "varA2");
[385](https://docs.rs#385)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarB.to_string(), "varb");
[386](https://docs.rs#386)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarC.to_string(), "VARC");
[387](https://docs.rs#387)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarD.to_string(), "var_d");
[388](https://docs.rs#388)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarE.to_string(), "VAR_E");
[389](https://docs.rs#389)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarF.to_string(), "varF");
[390](https://docs.rs#390)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarG1.to_string(), "VarG1");
[391](https://docs.rs#391)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::varG2.to_string(), "VarG2");
[392](https://docs.rs#392)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarH.to_string(), "var-h");
[393](https://docs.rs#393)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarI.to_string(), "VAR-I");
[394](https://docs.rs#394)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarJ.to_string(), "Var J");
[395](https://docs.rs#395)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarK.to_string(), "Var k");
[396](https://docs.rs#396)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarL.to_string(), "var l");
[397](https://docs.rs#397)/// assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarM.to_string(), "VAR M");
[398](https://docs.rs#398)/// ```
[399](https://docs.rs#399)///
[400](https://docs.rs#400)/// ## `#[display(opt)]`
[401](https://docs.rs#401)///
[402](https://docs.rs#402)/// When applied to an `Option<T>` field, this attribute makes the field display an empty string for `None` and use `T`'s trait implementations directly (not `Option<T>`'s, but `T`'s `Display`, `FromStr`, etc.) for `Some(T)`.
[403](https://docs.rs#403)///
[404](https://docs.rs#404)/// ```rust
[405](https://docs.rs#405)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[406](https://docs.rs#406)///
[407](https://docs.rs#407)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[408](https://docs.rs#408)/// struct X {
[409](https://docs.rs#409)///     #[display("a={}", opt)]
[410](https://docs.rs#410)///     a: Option<u32>,
[411](https://docs.rs#411)/// }
[412](https://docs.rs#412)/// assert_eq!(X { a: Some(10) }.to_string(), "a=10");
[413](https://docs.rs#413)/// assert_eq!(X { a: None::<u32> }.to_string(), "");
[414](https://docs.rs#414)/// ```
[415](https://docs.rs#415)///
[416](https://docs.rs#416)/// When the field is `None`, not just the placeholder but the entire format string for that field is omitted from the output. In the example above, when `a` is `None`, the output is `""` rather than `"a="`.
[417](https://docs.rs#417)///
[418](https://docs.rs#418)/// ## `#[display(with = "...")]`, `#[from_str(with = "...")]`
[419](https://docs.rs#419)///
[420](https://docs.rs#420)/// You can customize [`Display`] and [`FromStr`] processing for a field by specifying the values that implements [`DisplayFormat`] and [`FromStrFormat`].
[421](https://docs.rs#421)///
[422](https://docs.rs#422)/// ```rust
[423](https://docs.rs#423)/// use parse_display::{Display, DisplayFormat, FromStr, FromStrFormat};
[424](https://docs.rs#424)///
[425](https://docs.rs#425)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[426](https://docs.rs#426)/// pub struct X {
[427](https://docs.rs#427)///     #[display(with = Plus1)]
[428](https://docs.rs#428)///     a: i32,
[429](https://docs.rs#429)/// }
[430](https://docs.rs#430)///
[431](https://docs.rs#431)/// struct Plus1;
[432](https://docs.rs#432)///
[433](https://docs.rs#433)/// impl DisplayFormat<i32> for Plus1 {
[434](https://docs.rs#434)///     fn write(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter, value: &i32) -> std::fmt::Result {
[435](https://docs.rs#435)///         write!(f, "{}", value + 1)
[436](https://docs.rs#436)///     }
[437](https://docs.rs#437)/// }
[438](https://docs.rs#438)/// impl FromStrFormat<i32> for Plus1 {
[439](https://docs.rs#439)///     type Err = <i32 as std::str::FromStr>::Err;
[440](https://docs.rs#440)///     fn parse(&self, s: &str) -> std::result::Result<i32, Self::Err> {
[441](https://docs.rs#441)///         Ok(s.parse::<i32>()? - 1)
[442](https://docs.rs#442)///     }
[443](https://docs.rs#443)/// }
[444](https://docs.rs#444)///
[445](https://docs.rs#445)/// assert_eq!(X { a: 1 }.to_string(), "2");
[446](https://docs.rs#446)/// assert_eq!("2".parse(), Ok(X { a: 1 }));
[447](https://docs.rs#447)/// ```
[448](https://docs.rs#448)///
[449](https://docs.rs#449)/// The expression specified for `with = ...` must be lightweight because it is called each time when formatting and parsing.
[450](https://docs.rs#450)///
[451](https://docs.rs#451)/// ## `#[display(bound(...))]`, `#[from_str(bound(...))]`
[452](https://docs.rs#452)///
[453](https://docs.rs#453)/// By default, the type of field used in the format is added to the trait bound.
[454](https://docs.rs#454)///
[455](https://docs.rs#455)/// In Rust prior to 1.59, this behavior causes a compile error if you use fields of non public type in public struct.
[456](https://docs.rs#456)///
[457](https://docs.rs#457)/// ```rust
[458](https://docs.rs#458)/// #![deny(private_in_public)]
[459](https://docs.rs#459)/// use parse_display::Display;
[460](https://docs.rs#460)///
[461](https://docs.rs#461)/// // private type `Inner<T>` in public interface (error E0446)
[462](https://docs.rs#462)/// #[derive(Display)]
[463](https://docs.rs#463)/// pub struct Outer<T>(Inner<T>);
[464](https://docs.rs#464)///
[465](https://docs.rs#465)/// #[derive(Display)]
[466](https://docs.rs#466)/// struct Inner<T>(T);
[467](https://docs.rs#467)/// ```
[468](https://docs.rs#468)///
[469](https://docs.rs#469)/// By writing `#[display(bound(...))]`, you can override the default behavior.
[470](https://docs.rs#470)///
[471](https://docs.rs#471)/// ### Specify trait bound type
[472](https://docs.rs#472)///
[473](https://docs.rs#473)/// By specifying the type, you can specify the type that need to implement `Display` and `FromStr`.
[474](https://docs.rs#474)///
[475](https://docs.rs#475)/// ```rust
[476](https://docs.rs#476)/// use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
[477](https://docs.rs#477)///
[478](https://docs.rs#478)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[479](https://docs.rs#479)/// #[display(bound(T))]
[480](https://docs.rs#480)/// pub struct Outer<T>(Inner<T>);
[481](https://docs.rs#481)///
[482](https://docs.rs#482)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[483](https://docs.rs#483)/// struct Inner<T>(T);
[484](https://docs.rs#484)///
[485](https://docs.rs#485)/// assert_eq!(Outer(Inner(10)).to_string(), "10");
[486](https://docs.rs#486)/// assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(Outer(Inner(10))));
[487](https://docs.rs#487)/// ```
[488](https://docs.rs#488)///
[489](https://docs.rs#489)/// ### Specify where predicate
[490](https://docs.rs#490)///
[491](https://docs.rs#491)/// You can also specify the where predicate.
[492](https://docs.rs#492)///
[493](https://docs.rs#493)/// ```rust
[494](https://docs.rs#494)/// use parse_display::Display;
[495](https://docs.rs#495)///
[496](https://docs.rs#496)/// #[derive(Display)]
[497](https://docs.rs#497)/// #[display(bound(T : std::fmt::Debug))]
[498](https://docs.rs#498)/// pub struct Outer<T>(Inner<T>);
[499](https://docs.rs#499)///
[500](https://docs.rs#500)/// #[derive(Display)]
[501](https://docs.rs#501)/// #[display("{0:?}")]
[502](https://docs.rs#502)/// struct Inner<T>(T);
[503](https://docs.rs#503)///
[504](https://docs.rs#504)/// assert_eq!(Outer(Inner(10)).to_string(), "10");
[505](https://docs.rs#505)/// ```
[506](https://docs.rs#506)///
[507](https://docs.rs#507)/// ### No trait bounds
[508](https://docs.rs#508)///
[509](https://docs.rs#509)/// You can also remove all trait bounds.
[510](https://docs.rs#510)///
[511](https://docs.rs#511)/// ```rust
[512](https://docs.rs#512)/// use parse_display::Display;
[513](https://docs.rs#513)///
[514](https://docs.rs#514)/// #[derive(Display)]
[515](https://docs.rs#515)/// #[display(bound())]
[516](https://docs.rs#516)/// pub struct Outer<T>(Inner<T>);
[517](https://docs.rs#517)///
[518](https://docs.rs#518)/// #[derive(Display)]
[519](https://docs.rs#519)/// #[display("ABC")]
[520](https://docs.rs#520)/// struct Inner<T>(T);
[521](https://docs.rs#521)///
[522](https://docs.rs#522)/// assert_eq!(Outer(Inner(10)).to_string(), "ABC");
[523](https://docs.rs#523)/// ```
[524](https://docs.rs#524)///
[525](https://docs.rs#525)/// ### Default trait bounds
[526](https://docs.rs#526)///
[527](https://docs.rs#527)/// `..` means default (automatically generated) trait bounds.
[528](https://docs.rs#528)///
[529](https://docs.rs#529)/// The following example specifies `T1` as a trait bound in addition to the default trait bound `T2`.
[530](https://docs.rs#530)///
[531](https://docs.rs#531)/// ```rust
[532](https://docs.rs#532)/// use parse_display::Display;
[533](https://docs.rs#533)///
[534](https://docs.rs#534)/// pub struct Inner<T>(T);
[535](https://docs.rs#535)///
[536](https://docs.rs#536)/// #[derive(Display)]
[537](https://docs.rs#537)/// #[display("{0.0}, {1}", bound(T1, ..))]
[538](https://docs.rs#538)/// pub struct Outer<T1, T2>(Inner<T1>, T2);
[539](https://docs.rs#539)///
[540](https://docs.rs#540)/// assert_eq!(Outer(Inner(10), 20).to_string(), "10, 20");
[541](https://docs.rs#541)/// ```
[542](https://docs.rs#542)///
[543](https://docs.rs#543)/// You can use a different trait bound for `Display` and `FromStr` by specifying both `#[display(bound(...))]` and `#[from_str(bound(...))]`.
[544](https://docs.rs#544)///
[545](https://docs.rs#545)/// ```rust
[546](https://docs.rs#546)/// use parse_display::*;
[547](https://docs.rs#547)/// use std::{fmt::Display, str::FromStr};
[548](https://docs.rs#548)///
[549](https://docs.rs#549)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[550](https://docs.rs#550)/// #[display(bound("T : Display"))]
[551](https://docs.rs#551)/// #[from_str(bound("T : FromStr"))]
[552](https://docs.rs#552)/// pub struct Outer<T>(Inner<T>);
[553](https://docs.rs#553)///
[554](https://docs.rs#554)/// #[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[555](https://docs.rs#555)/// struct Inner<T>(T);
[556](https://docs.rs#556)///
[557](https://docs.rs#557)/// assert_eq!(Outer(Inner(10)).to_string(), "10");
[558](https://docs.rs#558)/// assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(Outer(Inner(10))));
[559](https://docs.rs#559)/// ```
[560](https://docs.rs#560)///
[561](https://docs.rs#561)/// ## `#[display(crate = ...)]`
[562](https://docs.rs#562)///
[563](https://docs.rs#563)/// Specify a path to the `parse-display` crate instance.
[564](https://docs.rs#564)///
[565](https://docs.rs#565)/// Used when `::parse_display` is not an instance of `parse-display`, such as when a macro is re-exported or used from another macro.
[566](https://docs.rs#566)///
[567](https://docs.rs#567)/// ## `#[display(dump)]`, `#[from_str(dump)]`
[568](https://docs.rs#568)///
[569](https://docs.rs#569)/// Outputs the generated code as a compile error.
[570](https://docs.rs#570)///
[571](https://docs.rs#571)/// ## `#[from_str(regex = "...")]`
[572](https://docs.rs#572)///
[573](https://docs.rs#573)/// Specify the format of the string to be input with `FromStr`.
[574](https://docs.rs#574)/// `#[display("...")]` is ignored, when this attribute is specified.
[575](https://docs.rs#575)///
[576](https://docs.rs#576)/// ### Capture name
[577](https://docs.rs#577)///
[578](https://docs.rs#578)/// The capture name corresponds to the field name.
[579](https://docs.rs#579)///
[580](https://docs.rs#580)/// ```rust
[581](https://docs.rs#581)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[582](https://docs.rs#582)///
[583](https://docs.rs#583)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[584](https://docs.rs#584)/// #[from_str(regex = "(?<a>[0-9]+)__(?<b>[0-9]+)")]
[585](https://docs.rs#585)/// struct MyStruct {
[586](https://docs.rs#586)///   a: u8,
[587](https://docs.rs#587)///   b: u8,
[588](https://docs.rs#588)/// }
[589](https://docs.rs#589)///
[590](https://docs.rs#590)/// assert_eq!("10__20".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a: 10, b: 20 }));
[591](https://docs.rs#591)/// ```
[592](https://docs.rs#592)///
[593](https://docs.rs#593)/// ### Field regex
[594](https://docs.rs#594)///
[595](https://docs.rs#595)/// Set `#[display("...")]` to struct and set `#[from_str(regex = "...")]` to field, regex is used in the position where field name is specified in `#[display("...")]`.
[596](https://docs.rs#596)///
[597](https://docs.rs#597)/// ```rust
[598](https://docs.rs#598)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[599](https://docs.rs#599)///
[600](https://docs.rs#600)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[601](https://docs.rs#601)/// #[display("{a}__{b}")]
[602](https://docs.rs#602)/// struct MyStruct {
[603](https://docs.rs#603)///   #[from_str(regex = "[0-9]+")]
[604](https://docs.rs#604)///   a: u8,
[605](https://docs.rs#605)///
[606](https://docs.rs#606)///   #[from_str(regex = "[0-9]+")]
[607](https://docs.rs#607)///   b: u8,
[608](https://docs.rs#608)/// }
[609](https://docs.rs#609)/// assert_eq!("10__20".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a: 10, b: 20 }));
[610](https://docs.rs#610)/// ```
[611](https://docs.rs#611)///
[612](https://docs.rs#612)/// If `#[from_str(regex = "...")]` is not set to field ,
[613](https://docs.rs#613)/// it operates in the same way as when `#[from_str(regex = "(?s:.*?)")]` is set.
[614](https://docs.rs#614)///
[615](https://docs.rs#615)/// ```rust
[616](https://docs.rs#616)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[617](https://docs.rs#617)///
[618](https://docs.rs#618)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[619](https://docs.rs#619)/// #[display("{a}{b}")]
[620](https://docs.rs#620)/// struct MyStruct {
[621](https://docs.rs#621)///   a: String,
[622](https://docs.rs#622)///   b: String,
[623](https://docs.rs#623)/// }
[624](https://docs.rs#624)/// assert_eq!("abcdef".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a:"".into(), b:"abcdef".into() }));
[625](https://docs.rs#625)/// ```
[626](https://docs.rs#626)///
[627](https://docs.rs#627)/// ### Field regex with capture
[628](https://docs.rs#628)///
[629](https://docs.rs#629)/// Using a named capture group with an empty name in the field's regex will convert only the string within that group to the field's value.
[630](https://docs.rs#630)///
[631](https://docs.rs#631)/// ```rust
[632](https://docs.rs#632)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[633](https://docs.rs#633)///
[634](https://docs.rs#634)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[635](https://docs.rs#635)/// struct MyStruct {
[636](https://docs.rs#636)///   #[from_str(regex = "a = (?<>[0-9]+)")]
[637](https://docs.rs#637)///   a: u8,
[638](https://docs.rs#638)/// }
[639](https://docs.rs#639)/// assert_eq!("a = 10".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a: 10 }));
[640](https://docs.rs#640)/// ```
[641](https://docs.rs#641)///
[642](https://docs.rs#642)/// ### Field regex with display format
[643](https://docs.rs#643)///
[644](https://docs.rs#644)/// If both `#[display("...")]` and `#[from_str(regex = "...")]` are specified for a field and the regex does not contain named capture groups, the pattern within the `{}` part of the format specified by `#[display("...")]` will be determined by `#[from_str(regex = "...")]`.
[645](https://docs.rs#645)///
[646](https://docs.rs#646)/// ```rust
[647](https://docs.rs#647)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[648](https://docs.rs#648)///
[649](https://docs.rs#649)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[650](https://docs.rs#650)/// struct X {
[651](https://docs.rs#651)///   #[display("a = {}")]
[652](https://docs.rs#652)///   #[from_str(regex = "[0-9]+")]
[653](https://docs.rs#653)///   a: u8,
[654](https://docs.rs#654)/// }
[655](https://docs.rs#655)/// assert_eq!("a = 10".parse(), Ok(X { a: 10 }));
[656](https://docs.rs#656)/// ```
[657](https://docs.rs#657)///
[658](https://docs.rs#658)/// If the regex does not contain named capture groups, `#[display("...")]` is ignored.
[659](https://docs.rs#659)///
[660](https://docs.rs#660)/// ```rust
[661](https://docs.rs#661)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[662](https://docs.rs#662)///
[663](https://docs.rs#663)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[664](https://docs.rs#664)/// struct Y {
[665](https://docs.rs#665)///   #[display("a = {}")]
[666](https://docs.rs#666)///   #[from_str(regex = "a = (?<>[0-9]+)")]
[667](https://docs.rs#667)///   a: u8,
[668](https://docs.rs#668)/// }
[669](https://docs.rs#669)/// assert_eq!("a = 10".parse(), Ok(Y { a: 10 }));
[670](https://docs.rs#670)/// assert!("a = a = 10".parse::<Y>().is_err());
[671](https://docs.rs#671)/// ```
[672](https://docs.rs#672)///
[673](https://docs.rs#673)/// ### Variant name
[674](https://docs.rs#674)///
[675](https://docs.rs#675)/// In the regex specified for enum or variant, empty name capture means variant name.
[676](https://docs.rs#676)///
[677](https://docs.rs#677)/// ```rust
[678](https://docs.rs#678)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[679](https://docs.rs#679)///
[680](https://docs.rs#680)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[681](https://docs.rs#681)/// #[from_str(regex = "___(?<>)___")]
[682](https://docs.rs#682)/// enum MyEnum {
[683](https://docs.rs#683)///   VarA,
[684](https://docs.rs#684)///
[685](https://docs.rs#685)///   #[from_str(regex = "xxx(?<>)xxx")]
[686](https://docs.rs#686)///   VarB,
[687](https://docs.rs#687)/// }
[688](https://docs.rs#688)/// assert_eq!("___VarA___".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
[689](https://docs.rs#689)/// assert_eq!("xxxVarBxxx".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarB));
[690](https://docs.rs#690)/// ```
[691](https://docs.rs#691)///
[692](https://docs.rs#692)/// ### Regex nested field
[693](https://docs.rs#693)///
[694](https://docs.rs#694)/// You can use nested field in regex.
[695](https://docs.rs#695)///
[696](https://docs.rs#696)/// ```rust
[697](https://docs.rs#697)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[698](https://docs.rs#698)///
[699](https://docs.rs#699)/// #[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Default)]
[700](https://docs.rs#700)/// struct X {
[701](https://docs.rs#701)///     a: u32,
[702](https://docs.rs#702)/// }
[703](https://docs.rs#703)///
[704](https://docs.rs#704)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[705](https://docs.rs#705)/// #[from_str(regex = "___(?<x.a>[0-9]+)")]
[706](https://docs.rs#706)/// struct Y {
[707](https://docs.rs#707)///     #[from_str(default)]
[708](https://docs.rs#708)///     x: X,
[709](https://docs.rs#709)/// }
[710](https://docs.rs#710)/// assert_eq!("___10".parse(), Ok(Y { x: X { a: 10 } }));
[711](https://docs.rs#711)/// ```
[712](https://docs.rs#712)///
[713](https://docs.rs#713)/// When using nested field, you need to use [`#[from_str(default)]`](#from_strdefault).
[714](https://docs.rs#714)///
[715](https://docs.rs#715)/// ### Regex priority
[716](https://docs.rs#716)///
[717](https://docs.rs#717)/// In addition to `#[from_str(regex = "...")]`,
[718](https://docs.rs#718)/// you can also specify `#[from_str(with = ...)]`, `#[display(with = ...)]`, or `#[from_str(regex_infer)]` to change the regular expression.
[719](https://docs.rs#719)/// If you specify multiple attributes in the same field, the regular expression that is applied is determined by the following priority.
[720](https://docs.rs#720)///
[721](https://docs.rs#721)/// - [`#[from_str(regex = "...")]`](#from_strregex--)
[722](https://docs.rs#722)/// - [`#[from_str(with = ...)]`, `#[display(with = ...)]`)](#displaywith---from_strwith--)
[723](https://docs.rs#723)/// - [`#[from_str(regex_infer)]`](#from_strregex_infer)
[724](https://docs.rs#724)///
[725](https://docs.rs#725)/// ## `#[from_str(regex_infer)]`
[726](https://docs.rs#726)///
[727](https://docs.rs#727)/// By default, fields are matched using the regular expression `(?s:.*?)`.
[728](https://docs.rs#728)///
[729](https://docs.rs#729)/// If you specify `#[from_str(regex_infer)]`,
[730](https://docs.rs#730)/// this behavior is changed and the pattern obtained from the field type's [`FromStrRegex`] is used for matching.
[731](https://docs.rs#731)///
[732](https://docs.rs#732)/// ```rust
[733](https://docs.rs#733)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[734](https://docs.rs#734)///
[735](https://docs.rs#735)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[736](https://docs.rs#736)/// #[display("{a}{b}")]
[737](https://docs.rs#737)/// struct X {
[738](https://docs.rs#738)///     a: u32,
[739](https://docs.rs#739)///     b: String,
[740](https://docs.rs#740)/// }
[741](https://docs.rs#741)///
[742](https://docs.rs#742)/// // `a` matches "" and `b` matches "1a", so it fails to convert to `Y`.
[743](https://docs.rs#743)/// assert!("1a".parse::<X>().is_err());
[744](https://docs.rs#744)///
[745](https://docs.rs#745)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[746](https://docs.rs#746)/// #[display("{a}{b}")]
[747](https://docs.rs#747)/// struct Y {
[748](https://docs.rs#748)///     #[from_str(regex_infer)]
[749](https://docs.rs#749)///     a: u32,
[750](https://docs.rs#750)///     b: String,
[751](https://docs.rs#751)/// }
[752](https://docs.rs#752)///
[753](https://docs.rs#753)/// // `a` matches "1" and `b` matches "a", so it can be converted to `Y`.
[754](https://docs.rs#754)/// assert_eq!("1a".parse(), Ok(Y { a: 1, b: "a".into() }));
[755](https://docs.rs#755)/// ```
[756](https://docs.rs#756)///
[757](https://docs.rs#757)/// If `#[from_str(regex_infer)]` is specified for a type or variant rather than a field, this attribute is applied to all fields.
[758](https://docs.rs#758)///
[759](https://docs.rs#759)/// ## `#[from_str(new = ...)]`
[760](https://docs.rs#760)///
[761](https://docs.rs#761)/// If `#[from_str(new = ...)]` is specified, the value will be initialized with the specified expression instead of the constructor.
[762](https://docs.rs#762)///
[763](https://docs.rs#763)/// The expression must return a value that implement [`IntoResult`] (e.g. `Self`, `Option<Self>`, `Result<Self, E>`).
[764](https://docs.rs#764)///
[765](https://docs.rs#765)/// In the expression, you can use a variable with the same name as the field name.
[766](https://docs.rs#766)///
[767](https://docs.rs#767)/// ```rust
[768](https://docs.rs#768)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[769](https://docs.rs#769)/// #[derive(FromStr, Debug, PartialEq)]
[770](https://docs.rs#770)/// #[from_str(new = Self::new(value))]
[771](https://docs.rs#771)/// struct MyNonZeroUSize {
[772](https://docs.rs#772)///     value: usize,
[773](https://docs.rs#773)/// }
[774](https://docs.rs#774)///
[775](https://docs.rs#775)/// impl MyNonZeroUSize {
[776](https://docs.rs#776)///     fn new(value: usize) -> Option<Self> {
[777](https://docs.rs#777)///         if value == 0 {
[778](https://docs.rs#778)///             None
[779](https://docs.rs#779)///         } else {
[780](https://docs.rs#780)///             Some(Self { value })
[781](https://docs.rs#781)///         }
[782](https://docs.rs#782)///     }
[783](https://docs.rs#783)/// }
[784](https://docs.rs#784)///
[785](https://docs.rs#785)/// assert_eq!("1".parse(), Ok(MyNonZeroUSize { value: 1 }));
[786](https://docs.rs#786)/// assert_eq!("0".parse::<MyNonZeroUSize>().is_err(), true);
[787](https://docs.rs#787)/// ```
[788](https://docs.rs#788)///
[789](https://docs.rs#789)/// In tuple struct, variables are named with a leading underscore and their index. (e.g. `_0`, `_1`).
[790](https://docs.rs#790)///
[791](https://docs.rs#791)/// ```rust
[792](https://docs.rs#792)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[793](https://docs.rs#793)/// #[derive(FromStr, Debug, PartialEq)]
[794](https://docs.rs#794)/// #[from_str(new = Self::new(_0))]
[795](https://docs.rs#795)/// struct MyNonZeroUSize(usize);
[796](https://docs.rs#796)///
[797](https://docs.rs#797)/// impl MyNonZeroUSize {
[798](https://docs.rs#798)///     fn new(value: usize) -> Option<Self> {
[799](https://docs.rs#799)///         if value == 0 {
[800](https://docs.rs#800)///             None
[801](https://docs.rs#801)///         } else {
[802](https://docs.rs#802)///             Some(Self(value))
[803](https://docs.rs#803)///         }
[804](https://docs.rs#804)///     }
[805](https://docs.rs#805)/// }
[806](https://docs.rs#806)///
[807](https://docs.rs#807)/// assert_eq!("1".parse(), Ok(MyNonZeroUSize(1)));
[808](https://docs.rs#808)/// assert_eq!("0".parse::<MyNonZeroUSize>().is_err(), true);
[809](https://docs.rs#809)/// ```
[810](https://docs.rs#810)///
[811](https://docs.rs#811)/// ## `#[from_str(ignore)]`
[812](https://docs.rs#812)///
[813](https://docs.rs#813)/// Specifying this attribute for a variant will not generate `FromStr` implementation for that variant.
[814](https://docs.rs#814)///
[815](https://docs.rs#815)/// ```rust
[816](https://docs.rs#816)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[817](https://docs.rs#817)///
[818](https://docs.rs#818)/// #[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
[819](https://docs.rs#819)/// struct CanNotFromStr;
[820](https://docs.rs#820)///
[821](https://docs.rs#821)/// #[derive(FromStr, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
[822](https://docs.rs#822)/// #[allow(dead_code)]
[823](https://docs.rs#823)/// enum HasIgnore {
[824](https://docs.rs#824)///     #[from_str(ignore)]
[825](https://docs.rs#825)///     A(CanNotFromStr),
[826](https://docs.rs#826)///     #[display("{0}")]
[827](https://docs.rs#827)///     B(u32),
[828](https://docs.rs#828)/// }
[829](https://docs.rs#829)///
[830](https://docs.rs#830)/// assert_eq!("1".parse(), Ok(HasIgnore::B(1)));
[831](https://docs.rs#831)/// ```
[832](https://docs.rs#832)///
[833](https://docs.rs#833)/// ## `#[from_str(default)]`
[834](https://docs.rs#834)///
[835](https://docs.rs#835)/// If this attribute is specified, the default value is used for fields not included in the input.
[836](https://docs.rs#836)///
[837](https://docs.rs#837)/// If an attribute is specified for struct, the struct's default value is used.
[838](https://docs.rs#838)///
[839](https://docs.rs#839)/// ```rust
[840](https://docs.rs#840)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[841](https://docs.rs#841)///
[842](https://docs.rs#842)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[843](https://docs.rs#843)/// #[display("{b}")]
[844](https://docs.rs#844)/// #[from_str(default)]
[845](https://docs.rs#845)/// struct MyStruct {
[846](https://docs.rs#846)///   a: u32,
[847](https://docs.rs#847)///   b: u32,
[848](https://docs.rs#848)/// }
[849](https://docs.rs#849)///
[850](https://docs.rs#850)/// impl Default for MyStruct {
[851](https://docs.rs#851)///   fn default() -> Self {
[852](https://docs.rs#852)///     Self { a:99, b:99 }
[853](https://docs.rs#853)///   }
[854](https://docs.rs#854)/// }
[855](https://docs.rs#855)/// assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a:99, b:10 }));
[856](https://docs.rs#856)/// ```
[857](https://docs.rs#857)///
[858](https://docs.rs#858)/// If an attribute is specified for field, the field type's default value is used.
[859](https://docs.rs#859)///
[860](https://docs.rs#860)/// ```rust
[861](https://docs.rs#861)/// use parse_display::FromStr;
[862](https://docs.rs#862)///
[863](https://docs.rs#863)/// #[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
[864](https://docs.rs#864)/// #[display("{b}")]
[865](https://docs.rs#865)/// struct MyStruct {
[866](https://docs.rs#866)///   #[from_str(default)]
[867](https://docs.rs#867)///   a: u32,
[868](https://docs.rs#868)///   b: u32,
[869](https://docs.rs#869)/// }
[870](https://docs.rs#870)///
[871](https://docs.rs#871)/// impl Default for MyStruct {
[872](https://docs.rs#872)///   fn default() -> Self {
[873](https://docs.rs#873)///     Self { a:99, b:99 }
[874](https://docs.rs#874)///   }
[875](https://docs.rs#875)/// }
[876](https://docs.rs#876)/// assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a:0, b:10 }));
[877](https://docs.rs#877)/// ```
[878](https://docs.rs#878)///
[879](https://docs.rs#879)/// ## Deprecated features
[880](https://docs.rs#880)///
[881](https://docs.rs#881)/// The following deprecated features will be removed in a future version.
[882](https://docs.rs#882)///
[883](https://docs.rs#883)/// | feature | description |
[884](https://docs.rs#884)/// | ------- | ----------- |
[885](https://docs.rs#885)/// | [`#[from_str(default_fields(...))]`](https://docs.rs/parse-display/0.10.0/parse_display/derive.Display.html#from_strdefault_fields) | Sets default values for same-named fields across variants; use `#[from_str(default)]` instead. |

[951](https://docs.rs#951)/// Formatting method used in [`#[display(with = ...)]`](macro@Display#displaywith---from_strwith--).
[952](https://docs.rs#952)pub trait DisplayFormat<T: ?Sized> {

# Display in parse_display - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/parse-display/0.11.0/parse_display/derive.Display.html

```
#[derive(Display)]
{
    // Attributes available to this derive:
    #[display]
}
```
## Expand description

Derive [ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#helper-attributes)Helper attributes

`#[derive(Display)]` and `#[derive(FromStr)]` use common helper attributes.

- `#[derive(Display)]`use- `#[display]`.
- `#[derive(FromStr)]`use both- `#[display]`and- `#[from_str]`, with- `#[from_str]`having priority.

Helper attributes can be written in the following positions.

| attribute | `#[display]` | `#[from_str]` | struct | enum | variant | field |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `#[display("...")]` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | |
| `#[display(style = "...")]` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | |||
| `#[display(with = ...)]` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | |||
| `#[display(opt)]` | ✔ | |||||
| `#[display(bound(...))]` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |
| `#[display(crate = ...)]` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | |||
| `#[display(dump)]` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ||
| `#[from_str(regex = "...")]` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | |
| `#[from_str(regex_infer)]` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | |
| `#[from_str(new = ...)]` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | |||
| `#[from_str(ignore)]` | ✔ | ✔ | ||||
| `#[from_str(default)]` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ |

[§](https://docs.rs#display)`#[display("...")]`

Specifies the format using a syntax similar to [ std::format!()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/macro.format.html).

However, unlike `std::format!()`, `{}` has the following meaning.

| format | struct | enum | variant | field | description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `{a}`,`{b}`,`{1}` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | Use a field with the specified name. |
| `{}` | ✔ | ✔ | Use a variant name of enum. | ||
| `{}`,`{:x}`,`{:?}` | ✔ | Use the field itself. | |||
| `{:x}`,`{:?}` | ✔ | ✔ | Use format traits other than for`Display``self`. (e.g.,`LowerHex`)`Debug` | ||
| `{a.b.c}` | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | ✔ | Use a nested field. |

[§](https://docs.rs#struct-format)Struct format

By writing `#[display("..")]`, you can specify the format used by `Display` and `FromStr`.

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{a}-{b}")]
struct MyStruct {
  a: u32,
  b: u32,
}
assert_eq!(MyStruct { a:10, b:20 }.to_string(), "10-20");
assert_eq!("10-20".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a:10, b:20 }));
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{0}+{1}")]
struct MyTuple(u32, u32);
assert_eq!(MyTuple(10, 20).to_string(), "10+20");
assert_eq!("10+20".parse(), Ok(MyTuple(10, 20)));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#newtype-pattern)Newtype pattern

If the struct has only one field, the format can be omitted. In this case, the only field is used.

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
struct NewType(u32);
assert_eq!(NewType(10).to_string(), "10");
assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(NewType(10)));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#enum-format)Enum format

In enum, you can specify the format for each variant.

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
enum MyEnum {
  #[display("aaa")]
  VarA,
  #[display("bbb")]
  VarB,
}
assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA.to_string(), "aaa");
assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarB.to_string(), "bbb");
assert_eq!("aaa".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
assert_eq!("bbb".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarB));
```
In enum format, `{}` means variant name.
Variant name style (e.g. `snake_case`, `camelCase`, …) can be specified by [ #[from_str(style = "...")]](https://docs.rs#displaystyle--).

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
enum MyEnum {
  #[display("aaa-{}")]
  VarA,
  #[display("bbb-{}")]
  VarB,
}
assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA.to_string(), "aaa-VarA");
assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarB.to_string(), "bbb-VarB");
assert_eq!("aaa-VarA".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
assert_eq!("bbb-VarB".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarB));
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display(style = "snake_case")]
enum MyEnumSnake {
  #[display("{}")]
  VarA,
}
assert_eq!(MyEnumSnake::VarA.to_string(), "var_a");
assert_eq!("var_a".parse(), Ok(MyEnumSnake::VarA));
```
By writing a format on enum instead of variant, you can specify the format common to multiple variants.

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("xxx-{}")]
enum MyEnum {
  VarA,
  VarB,
}
assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA.to_string(), "xxx-VarA");
assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarB.to_string(), "xxx-VarB");
assert_eq!("xxx-VarA".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
assert_eq!("xxx-VarB".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarB));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#unit-variants)Unit variants

If all variants has no field, format can be omitted. In this case, variant name is used.

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
enum MyEnum {
  VarA,
  VarB,
}
assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA.to_string(), "VarA");
assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarB.to_string(), "VarB");
assert_eq!("VarA".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
assert_eq!("VarB".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarB));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#field-format)Field format

You can specify the format of the field.
In field format, `{}` means the field itself.

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{a}, {b}")]
struct MyStruct {
  #[display("a is {}")]
  a: u32,
  #[display("b is {}")]
  b: u32,
}
assert_eq!(MyStruct { a:10, b:20 }.to_string(), "a is 10, b is 20");
assert_eq!("a is 10, b is 20".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a:10, b:20 }));
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{0}, {1}")]
struct MyTuple(#[display("first is {}")] u32, #[display("next is {}")] u32);
assert_eq!(MyTuple(10, 20).to_string(), "first is 10, next is 20");
assert_eq!("first is 10, next is 20".parse(), Ok(MyTuple(10, 20)));
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
enum MyEnum {
  #[display("this is A {0}")]
  VarA(#[display("___{}___")] u32),
}
assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA(10).to_string(), "this is A ___10___");
assert_eq!("this is A ___10___".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA(10)));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#format-parameter)Format parameter

Like `std::format!()`, format parameter can be specified.

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{a:>04}")]
struct WithFormatParameter {
  a: u32,
}
assert_eq!(WithFormatParameter { a:5 }.to_string(), "0005");
```
When `{}` is used within `#[display("...")]` set for an enum, and if a format trait is added to `{}` such as `{:?}`, the meaning changes from “variant name” to “a string using a trait other than Display for self.”

```
use parse_display::Display;
#[derive(Display, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{}")]
enum X {
  A,
}
assert_eq!(X::A.to_string(), "A");
#[derive(Display, PartialEq)]
#[display("{:?}")]
enum Y {
  A,
}
impl std::fmt::Debug for Y {
  fn fmt(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter) -> std::fmt::Result {
    write!(f, "Debug Y")
  }
}
assert_eq!(Y::A.to_string(), "Debug Y");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#nested-field)Nested field

You can use nested field, e.g. `{x.a}` .

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Default)]
struct X {
    a: u32,
    b: u32,
}
#[derive(FromStr, Display, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{x.a}")]
struct Y {
    #[from_str(default)]
    x: X,
}
assert_eq!(Y { x: X { a: 10, b: 20 } }.to_string(), "10");
assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(Y { x: X { a: 10, b: 0 } }));
```
When using nested field, you need to use [ #[from_str(default)]](https://docs.rs#from_strdefault) to implement

`FromStr`.[§](https://docs.rs#displaystyle--)`#[display(style = "...")]`

By writing `#[display(style = "...")]`, you can specify the variant name style.
The following styles are available.

- `none`
- `lowercase`
- `UPPERCASE`
- `snake_case`
- `SNAKE_CASE`
- `camelCase`
- `CamelCase`
- `kebab-case`
- `KEBAB-CASE`
- `Title Case`
- `Title case`
- `title case`
- `TITLE CASE`

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display(style = "snake_case")]
enum MyEnum {
  VarA,
  VarB,
}
assert_eq!(MyEnum::VarA.to_string(), "var_a");
assert_eq!("var_a".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
enum StyleExample {
  #[display(style = "none")]
  VarA1,
  #[display(style = "none")]
  varA2,
  #[display(style = "lowercase")]
  VarB,
  #[display(style = "UPPERCASE")]
  VarC,
  #[display(style = "snake_case")]
  VarD,
  #[display(style = "SNAKE_CASE")]
  VarE,
  #[display(style = "camelCase")]
  VarF,
  #[display(style = "CamelCase")]
  VarG1,
  #[display(style = "CamelCase")]
  varG2,
  #[display(style = "kebab-case")]
  VarH,
  #[display(style = "KEBAB-CASE")]
  VarI,
  #[display(style = "Title Case")]
  VarJ,
  #[display(style = "Title case")]
  VarK,
  #[display(style = "title case")]
  VarL,
  #[display(style = "TITLE CASE")]
  VarM,
}
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarA1.to_string(), "VarA1");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::varA2.to_string(), "varA2");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarB.to_string(), "varb");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarC.to_string(), "VARC");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarD.to_string(), "var_d");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarE.to_string(), "VAR_E");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarF.to_string(), "varF");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarG1.to_string(), "VarG1");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::varG2.to_string(), "VarG2");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarH.to_string(), "var-h");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarI.to_string(), "VAR-I");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarJ.to_string(), "Var J");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarK.to_string(), "Var k");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarL.to_string(), "var l");
assert_eq!(StyleExample::VarM.to_string(), "VAR M");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#displayopt)`#[display(opt)]`

When applied to an `Option<T>` field, this attribute makes the field display an empty string for `None` and use `T`’s trait implementations directly (not `Option<T>`’s, but `T`’s `Display`, `FromStr`, etc.) for `Some(T)`.

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
struct X {
    #[display("a={}", opt)]
    a: Option<u32>,
}
assert_eq!(X { a: Some(10) }.to_string(), "a=10");
assert_eq!(X { a: None::<u32> }.to_string(), "");
```
When the field is `None`, not just the placeholder but the entire format string for that field is omitted from the output. In the example above, when `a` is `None`, the output is `""` rather than `"a="`.

[§](https://docs.rs#displaywith---from_strwith--)`#[display(with = "...")]`, `#[from_str(with = "...")]`

You can customize [ Display](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/fmt/trait.Display.html) and

[processing for a field by specifying the values that implements](https://docs.rs/derive.FromStr.html)

`FromStr`[and](https://docs.rs/trait.DisplayFormat.html)

`DisplayFormat`[.](https://docs.rs/trait.FromStrFormat.html)

`FromStrFormat````
use parse_display::{Display, DisplayFormat, FromStr, FromStrFormat};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
pub struct X {
    #[display(with = Plus1)]
    a: i32,
}
struct Plus1;
impl DisplayFormat<i32> for Plus1 {
    fn write(&self, f: &mut std::fmt::Formatter, value: &i32) -> std::fmt::Result {
        write!(f, "{}", value + 1)
    }
}
impl FromStrFormat<i32> for Plus1 {
    type Err = <i32 as std::str::FromStr>::Err;
    fn parse(&self, s: &str) -> std::result::Result<i32, Self::Err> {
        Ok(s.parse::<i32>()? - 1)
    }
}
assert_eq!(X { a: 1 }.to_string(), "2");
assert_eq!("2".parse(), Ok(X { a: 1 }));
```
The expression specified for `with = ...` must be lightweight because it is called each time when formatting and parsing.

[§](https://docs.rs#displaybound-from_strbound)`#[display(bound(...))]`, `#[from_str(bound(...))]`

By default, the type of field used in the format is added to the trait bound.

In Rust prior to 1.59, this behavior causes a compile error if you use fields of non public type in public struct.

```
#![deny(private_in_public)]
use parse_display::Display;
// private type `Inner<T>` in public interface (error E0446)
#[derive(Display)]
pub struct Outer<T>(Inner<T>);
#[derive(Display)]
struct Inner<T>(T);
```
By writing `#[display(bound(...))]`, you can override the default behavior.

[§](https://docs.rs#specify-trait-bound-type)Specify trait bound type

By specifying the type, you can specify the type that need to implement `Display` and `FromStr`.

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display(bound(T))]
pub struct Outer<T>(Inner<T>);
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
struct Inner<T>(T);
assert_eq!(Outer(Inner(10)).to_string(), "10");
assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(Outer(Inner(10))));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#specify-where-predicate)Specify where predicate

You can also specify the where predicate.

```
use parse_display::Display;
#[derive(Display)]
#[display(bound(T : std::fmt::Debug))]
pub struct Outer<T>(Inner<T>);
#[derive(Display)]
#[display("{0:?}")]
struct Inner<T>(T);
assert_eq!(Outer(Inner(10)).to_string(), "10");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#no-trait-bounds)No trait bounds

You can also remove all trait bounds.

```
use parse_display::Display;
#[derive(Display)]
#[display(bound())]
pub struct Outer<T>(Inner<T>);
#[derive(Display)]
#[display("ABC")]
struct Inner<T>(T);
assert_eq!(Outer(Inner(10)).to_string(), "ABC");
```
[§](https://docs.rs#default-trait-bounds)Default trait bounds

`..` means default (automatically generated) trait bounds.

The following example specifies `T1` as a trait bound in addition to the default trait bound `T2`.

```
use parse_display::Display;
pub struct Inner<T>(T);
#[derive(Display)]
#[display("{0.0}, {1}", bound(T1, ..))]
pub struct Outer<T1, T2>(Inner<T1>, T2);
assert_eq!(Outer(Inner(10), 20).to_string(), "10, 20");
```
You can use a different trait bound for `Display` and `FromStr` by specifying both `#[display(bound(...))]` and `#[from_str(bound(...))]`.

```
use parse_display::*;
use std::{fmt::Display, str::FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display(bound("T : Display"))]
#[from_str(bound("T : FromStr"))]
pub struct Outer<T>(Inner<T>);
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
struct Inner<T>(T);
assert_eq!(Outer(Inner(10)).to_string(), "10");
assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(Outer(Inner(10))));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#displaycrate--)`#[display(crate = ...)]`

Specify a path to the `parse-display` crate instance.

Used when `::parse_display` is not an instance of `parse-display`, such as when a macro is re-exported or used from another macro.

[§](https://docs.rs#displaydump-from_strdump)`#[display(dump)]`, `#[from_str(dump)]`

Outputs the generated code as a compile error.

[§](https://docs.rs#from_strregex--)`#[from_str(regex = "...")]`

Specify the format of the string to be input with `FromStr`.
`#[display("...")]` is ignored, when this attribute is specified.

[§](https://docs.rs#capture-name)Capture name

The capture name corresponds to the field name.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[from_str(regex = "(?<a>[0-9]+)__(?<b>[0-9]+)")]
struct MyStruct {
  a: u8,
  b: u8,
}
assert_eq!("10__20".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a: 10, b: 20 }));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#field-regex)Field regex

Set `#[display("...")]` to struct and set `#[from_str(regex = "...")]` to field, regex is used in the position where field name is specified in `#[display("...")]`.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{a}__{b}")]
struct MyStruct {
  #[from_str(regex = "[0-9]+")]
  a: u8,
  #[from_str(regex = "[0-9]+")]
  b: u8,
}
assert_eq!("10__20".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a: 10, b: 20 }));
```
If `#[from_str(regex = "...")]` is not set to field ,
it operates in the same way as when `#[from_str(regex = "(?s:.*?)")]` is set.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{a}{b}")]
struct MyStruct {
  a: String,
  b: String,
}
assert_eq!("abcdef".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a:"".into(), b:"abcdef".into() }));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#field-regex-with-capture)Field regex with capture

Using a named capture group with an empty name in the field’s regex will convert only the string within that group to the field’s value.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
struct MyStruct {
  #[from_str(regex = "a = (?<>[0-9]+)")]
  a: u8,
}
assert_eq!("a = 10".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a: 10 }));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#field-regex-with-display-format)Field regex with display format

If both `#[display("...")]` and `#[from_str(regex = "...")]` are specified for a field and the regex does not contain named capture groups, the pattern within the `{}` part of the format specified by `#[display("...")]` will be determined by `#[from_str(regex = "...")]`.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
struct X {
  #[display("a = {}")]
  #[from_str(regex = "[0-9]+")]
  a: u8,
}
assert_eq!("a = 10".parse(), Ok(X { a: 10 }));
```
If the regex does not contain named capture groups, `#[display("...")]` is ignored.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
struct Y {
  #[display("a = {}")]
  #[from_str(regex = "a = (?<>[0-9]+)")]
  a: u8,
}
assert_eq!("a = 10".parse(), Ok(Y { a: 10 }));
assert!("a = a = 10".parse::<Y>().is_err());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#variant-name)Variant name

In the regex specified for enum or variant, empty name capture means variant name.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[from_str(regex = "___(?<>)___")]
enum MyEnum {
  VarA,
  #[from_str(regex = "xxx(?<>)xxx")]
  VarB,
}
assert_eq!("___VarA___".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarA));
assert_eq!("xxxVarBxxx".parse(), Ok(MyEnum::VarB));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#regex-nested-field)Regex nested field

You can use nested field in regex.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(PartialEq, Debug, Default)]
struct X {
    a: u32,
}
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[from_str(regex = "___(?<x.a>[0-9]+)")]
struct Y {
    #[from_str(default)]
    x: X,
}
assert_eq!("___10".parse(), Ok(Y { x: X { a: 10 } }));
```
When using nested field, you need to use [ #[from_str(default)]](https://docs.rs#from_strdefault).

[§](https://docs.rs#regex-priority)Regex priority

In addition to `#[from_str(regex = "...")]`,
you can also specify `#[from_str(with = ...)]`, `#[display(with = ...)]`, or `#[from_str(regex_infer)]` to change the regular expression.
If you specify multiple attributes in the same field, the regular expression that is applied is determined by the following priority.

- `#[from_str(regex = "...")]`
- `#[from_str(with = ...)]`,- `#[display(with = ...)]`)
- `#[from_str(regex_infer)]`

[§](https://docs.rs#from_strregex_infer)`#[from_str(regex_infer)]`

By default, fields are matched using the regular expression `(?s:.*?)`.

If you specify `#[from_str(regex_infer)]`,
this behavior is changed and the pattern obtained from the field type’s [ FromStrRegex](https://docs.rs/trait.FromStrRegex.html) is used for matching.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{a}{b}")]
struct X {
    a: u32,
    b: String,
}
// `a` matches "" and `b` matches "1a", so it fails to convert to `Y`.
assert!("1a".parse::<X>().is_err());
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{a}{b}")]
struct Y {
    #[from_str(regex_infer)]
    a: u32,
    b: String,
}
// `a` matches "1" and `b` matches "a", so it can be converted to `Y`.
assert_eq!("1a".parse(), Ok(Y { a: 1, b: "a".into() }));
```
If `#[from_str(regex_infer)]` is specified for a type or variant rather than a field, this attribute is applied to all fields.

[§](https://docs.rs#from_strnew--)`#[from_str(new = ...)]`

If `#[from_str(new = ...)]` is specified, the value will be initialized with the specified expression instead of the constructor.

The expression must return a value that implement [ IntoResult](https://docs.rs/trait.IntoResult.html) (e.g.

`Self`, `Option<Self>`, `Result<Self, E>`).In the expression, you can use a variable with the same name as the field name.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, Debug, PartialEq)]
#[from_str(new = Self::new(value))]
struct MyNonZeroUSize {
    value: usize,
}
impl MyNonZeroUSize {
    fn new(value: usize) -> Option<Self> {
        if value == 0 {
            None
        } else {
            Some(Self { value })
        }
    }
}
assert_eq!("1".parse(), Ok(MyNonZeroUSize { value: 1 }));
assert_eq!("0".parse::<MyNonZeroUSize>().is_err(), true);
```
In tuple struct, variables are named with a leading underscore and their index. (e.g. `_0`, `_1`).

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, Debug, PartialEq)]
#[from_str(new = Self::new(_0))]
struct MyNonZeroUSize(usize);
impl MyNonZeroUSize {
    fn new(value: usize) -> Option<Self> {
        if value == 0 {
            None
        } else {
            Some(Self(value))
        }
    }
}
assert_eq!("1".parse(), Ok(MyNonZeroUSize(1)));
assert_eq!("0".parse::<MyNonZeroUSize>().is_err(), true);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#from_strignore)`#[from_str(ignore)]`

Specifying this attribute for a variant will not generate `FromStr` implementation for that variant.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
struct CanNotFromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
#[allow(dead_code)]
enum HasIgnore {
    #[from_str(ignore)]
    A(CanNotFromStr),
    #[display("{0}")]
    B(u32),
}
assert_eq!("1".parse(), Ok(HasIgnore::B(1)));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#from_strdefault)`#[from_str(default)]`

If this attribute is specified, the default value is used for fields not included in the input.

If an attribute is specified for struct, the struct’s default value is used.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{b}")]
#[from_str(default)]
struct MyStruct {
  a: u32,
  b: u32,
}
impl Default for MyStruct {
  fn default() -> Self {
    Self { a:99, b:99 }
  }
}
assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a:99, b:10 }));
```
If an attribute is specified for field, the field type’s default value is used.

```
use parse_display::FromStr;
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{b}")]
struct MyStruct {
  #[from_str(default)]
  a: u32,
  b: u32,
}
impl Default for MyStruct {
  fn default() -> Self {
    Self { a:99, b:99 }
  }
}
assert_eq!("10".parse(), Ok(MyStruct { a:0, b:10 }));
```
[§](https://docs.rs#deprecated-features)Deprecated features

The following deprecated features will be removed in a future version.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/parse_display/lib.rs.html#1026-1028)#### fn [regex_pattern](https://docs.rs#method.regex_pattern)(&self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/parse_display/lib.rs.html#1026-1028)

#### fn [regex_pattern](https://docs.rs#method.regex_pattern)(&self) -> [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

**crate feature**only.

`std`Return a regular expression that the input string needs to match.

By default, [ ANY_REGEX](https://docs.rs/constant.ANY_REGEX.html) is returned, which matches any string.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use parse_display::{FromStr, FromStrFormat};
struct Number;
impl FromStrFormat<String> for Number {
    type Err = <String as std::str::FromStr>::Err;
    fn parse(&self, s: &str) -> std::result::Result<String, Self::Err> {
        s.parse()
    }
    fn regex_pattern(&self) -> String {
        r"[0-9]+".into()
    }
}
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{0}{1}")]
struct X(String, String);
#[derive(FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{0}{1}")]
struct Y(#[from_str(with = Number)] String, String);
assert_eq!("123abc".parse(), Ok(X("".into(), "123abc".into())));
assert_eq!("123abc".parse(), Ok(Y("123".into(), "abc".into())));
```
If the field type includes type parameters, the regex must be the same regardless of the type parameters.

If the regex differs, it will panic in debug mode and result in an incorrect parse in release mode.

```
use parse_display::{FromStr, FromStrFormat ,ParseError};
use std::any::{type_name, Any};
use std::str::FromStr;
struct TypeNameFormat;
impl<T: Default + Any> FromStrFormat<T> for TypeNameFormat {
    type Err = ParseError;
    fn parse(&self, _s: &str) -> core::result::Result<T, Self::Err> {
        Ok(Default::default())
    }
    fn regex_pattern(&self) -> String {
        type_name::<T>().to_string()
    }
}
#[derive(FromStr)]
struct X<T: Default + std::any::Any>(#[from_str(with = TypeNameFormat)] T);
let _ = X::<u32>::from_str("u32");
let _ = X::<u16>::from_str("u16"); // panic on debug mode
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/parse_display/lib.rs.html#1033-1035)

use `regex_pattern` instead.
In `regex_pattern`, use `ANY_REGEX` instead of `None` for patterns that matches any string.

**crate feature**only.

# parse_display - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/parse-display/latest/parse_display/

## Expand description

This crate provides derive macro `Display` and `FromStr`.
These macros use common helper attributes to specify the format.

See [ #[derive(Display)]](https://docs.rs/derive.Display.html) for details.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use parse_display::{Display, FromStr};
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display("{a}-{b}")]
struct X {
  a: u32,
  b: u32,
}
assert_eq!(X { a:10, b:20 }.to_string(), "10-20");
assert_eq!("10-20".parse(), Ok(X { a:10, b:20 }));
#[derive(Display, FromStr, PartialEq, Debug)]
#[display(style = "snake_case")]
enum Y {
  VarA,
  VarB,
}
assert_eq!(Y::VarA.to_string(), "var_a");
assert_eq!("var_a".parse(), Ok(Y::VarA));
```
